definitions.explanation: An honorific title for a highly skilled and respected painter or artist. Can also be used humorously or sarcastically to describe someone who draws, regardless of skill.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{日本画|にほんが}の{画伯|がはく}だ。
examples.english: He is a master of Japanese-style painting.

examples.japanese: {画伯|がはく}の{作品|さくひん}が{美術館|びじゅつかん}に{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: The master painter's works are on display at the museum.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{描|か}いた{絵|え}を{見|み}て、「さすが{画伯|がはく}」と{冗談|じょうだん}を{言|い}った。
examples.english: Looking at the child's drawing, I jokingly said, 'What a master painter!'

notes:
{画伯|がはく} is an honorific title for a highly skilled and respected painter. It combines {画|が} (painting) + {伯|はく} (chief, elder).

USAGE:
Originally a respectful title for accomplished painters, similar to 'master painter.' In modern usage, it has developed a humorous or ironic use, especially online and among younger speakers, to refer to anyone who draws — even jokingly when the drawing is not particularly skilled.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {画伯|がはく}の{作品|さくひん} (the master's works)
- {画伯|がはく}と{呼|よ}ばれる (to be called a master painter)
- ○○{画伯|がはく} (Master [Name] — used as a title after a name)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {画家|がか}: painter, artist (neutral, standard term)
- {巨匠|きょしょう}: master, maestro (broader, not limited to painting)
- {画伯|がはく} carries more respect or formality than {画家|がか}, but its ironic use is now very common

REGISTER:
Formal when used seriously; playful or ironic in casual/internet contexts.
